To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the compositionality of a model is a very important property for the efficiency of model checking, and that the efficiency of model-checking can be improved significantly by using dependency analysis.
the use of compositionality and dependency reduction in model checking of state machines is an effective technique for improving verification efficiency.

1) the state/event model checker can verify a large number of state/event models that were previously intractable; 2) the state/event models can be verified in less time than required to simulate them; 3) the state/event system is verified as one unit rather than as a collection of smaller components; and 4) the verification results are correct and useful for the design of embedded reactive systems.

the following questions: How do you verify the behavior of a large reactive system with a large number of states and events? compositionality and dependency are two orthogonal techniques that, when combined, can significantly improve the efficiency and scalability of symbolic model checking.
